minutes.headline: Board adopted a single FY2019 tax rate and chose not to call a special election for the vacant seat.
minutes.summary: The board reorganized after a member's resignation, held the continued tax classification hearing, and kept a uniform rate for all property classes. It filled the Charter Review seat by a contested vote, renewed annual licenses, and decided to stay at four members rather than hold a special election. The town manager reported on roads, recycling, the FY20 budget schedule and facilities.

what_happened.line: The Select Board set one FY2019 tax rate for all property classes, with a residential factor of 1.0, pending state Department of Revenue approval.
The board voted to stay at four members until the regular election rather than call a special election for the vacant seat.
The board named a vice chair and a clerk after a member's resignation, and ratified two DPW appointments.
The Charter Review Committee seat was filled by a contested vote; the minutes record the outcome as not audible.
The board approved 2019 alcohol license renewals as read and agreed to skip the December workshop, aiming for a joint January facilities meeting.

why_it_matters: A single rate means homes and businesses are taxed at the same rate per an amount as heard of value, and rising valuations mean the average residential bill still goes up even as the rate falls.

Staying at four members leaves the board without a fifth vote on any split decision until the regular election, in exchange for avoiding a special election that was estimated at a few thousand dollars.
The fire pumper truck was flagged in capital planning as needing a full appropriation to order, a request residents may be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
watch_next: State Department of Revenue approval of the FY2019 tax rates.
A joint January meeting on facilities with the historic commission, historical society and APDC, and a future agenda item on the open space endorsement request.
